details: Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, stated that Iran would target oil facilities, undersea cables, data centers, and AI facilities across seven Gulf countries if the U.S. and Israel launch new attacks. This marks the first time AI infrastructure has been explicitly named as a military target. Speculation about a renewed US-Israeli assault on Iran has driven Brent crude oil prices to $113.4 a barrel.
title: Iran Threatens Gulf Oil & AI Facilities Amid Renewed US-Israel Attack Speculation

details: The U.S. State Department ordered non-emergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia due to escalating attacks by Iranian-backed Houthi militants. Attacks on civilian airports and critical infrastructure have caused casualties and travel disruptions, leading to a rise in oil prices.
title: US Orders Diplomats to Leave Saudi Arabia Amid Escalating Houthi Attacks

details: The White House announced that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a local ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, Ukraine, starting October 29. The agreement, reportedly brokered by First Lady Melania Trump, aims to facilitate humanitarian aid delivery and civilian evacuations from the city, which faces severe shortages.
title: Russia and Ukraine Agree to Local Ceasefire in Oleshky

details: US tech stocks experienced a sharp decline, with the Nasdaq Composite falling 2.6%, due to investor concerns about the sustainability and profitability of massive capital investments in artificial intelligence. This sell-off was also influenced by rising oil prices.
title: US Tech Stocks Tumble as Investors Fret Over AI Spending

details: Global debt surged by $10 trillion in the first half of 2026, surpassing $365 trillion, according to the Institute of International Finance. Advanced economies spent over $3.3 trillion on government bond interest in the past year, exceeding global military spending. This rising debt burden and climbing interest costs are squeezing government budgets and fueling cost-of-living protests, particularly in Europe.
title: Global Debt Exceeds $365 Trillion, Interest Bill Climbing
